oneLine: Agent observability and self-healing platform: detects failures from traces, proposes a fix, and promotes it only if it passes the checks.

figures.label: LLM-written patches that broke an already-passing task
macro recall on a sealed 357-trace test split

problem: LLM agents fail quietly in production, and fixes written by an LLM can break things that already worked.
built: An 11-service reliability platform. Agents send traces through a fail-open pip SDK (nexus-llmops, 0.04 ms overhead) or OpenTelemetry; traces stream over Kafka to NLI + rule detectors for 5 failure types; a LangGraph critic proposes a config patch (about $0.03 per heal); a pre-registered gate with repair, held-out and regression checks decides whether the patch is promoted.
results: 1 in 4 LLM-written patches broke an already-passing task (12/48). The gate avoided the 6 false promotions a naive before/after check made, and 0 of its 25 promotions failed on fresh seeds.

On NexusBench (716 traces, 5 injected failure types, rule-derived labels, 72/72 hand-checked), macro recall rose from 0.29 to 0.96 on a sealed 357-trace test split; live false alerts on normal traces fell from 118/118 to 1/118.

label: Ongoing research · Fall 2026 · Graduate Research Assistant, UM–Dearborn
oneLine: Research verifier for LLM-generated code repairs on SWE-bench Verified.

figures.label: incorrect patches caught by existing tests

problem: Judging whether an AI agent's code fix is correct usually needs hidden tests, and real repositories don't have them.
built: An oracle-blind verifier that accepts, flags or rejects LLM-generated SWE-bench Verified patches using existing regression tests, static analysis and reproduction tests frozen before the patch is seen, all in network-isolated Docker.
results: Over 100 tasks, accepted patches were correct 87% of the time (47/54).

A pre-registered audit caught agents reading newer package copies baked into prebuilt images (8 of 50 tasks); I halted the study, added container masking and integrity checks, and reran all 100 tasks.
Rebuilding test execution with per-module isolation, retries and time budgets raised conclusive verdicts from 31 to 58 of 83 tasks (95% of 37.6K selected test runs now return a result).
The study also showed existing tests catch only 1 of 14 incorrect patches, and that SWE-bench's archived grades were bound to the wrong patch on 9 of 83 tasks. Backed by 1,100+ unit tests.

oneLine: Evidence-gated compatibility runtime for evolving AI agent tools.

figures.label: across the frozen benchmark and real migrations

problem: Backend tools change their schemas, and an AI agent's existing tool calls break.
built: A Model Context Protocol proxy that keeps an unchanged agent's tool calls working as tools evolve. Gemini-generated adapters are promoted only after independent replay and SQLite side-effect checks pass; it ships with a CLI and a live inspector.
results: On a frozen 195-record benchmark and 6 public MCP migrations, it recovered 2 migrations before targeted fixes, then Fabric 3/3 and Mapbox 2/3 after extending the adapter language, and safely rejected 2, with 0 false-compatible promotions.

figures.label: Gemma 4 E2B via LiteRT-LM, no network
per cited note on a phone CPU

problem: Health workers on home visits may have no connectivity, and their notes need to be accurate and traceable to protocol.
built: An offline Android maternal-health copilot that runs Gemma 4 E2B on-device via LiteRT-LM, turning a visit observation, patient history and retrieved protocol text into a cited, structured note. Every note passes a strict parser, a citation validator, a safety post-processor and health-worker review.
results: Cited notes in 15–22 s on a phone CPU, with no network; 300+ unit tests.
